newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Systemat plans stock market listing - paper.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Systemat plans stock market listing - paper.

text.p: Belgian computer distributor and service company Systemat-Daterelay is looking at listing on the Brussels Stock Exchange, its chief executive officer told newspaper L'Echo in an interview published on Friday.
"Systemat is favourably looking at the idea of going to the bourse to finance growth," CEO Jean-Claude Loge was quoted as saying.

Systemat distributes IBM, Compaq and Toshiba computers. It had sales in 1996 of around 3.5 billion francs and expects net profit to be around 75 million francs, more than double 30 million in 1995, L'Echo said.
L'Echo said the company aimed to double sales by 2000, achieving a gross profit margin on sales of three to four percent.
The size of the listing, which is being prepared by Belgian bank Banque Bruxelles Lambert, was not decided but existing shareholders aimed only to keep a "small majority" in the company, L'Echo said.
Loge was quoted as saying "putting 25 percent on the bourse does not make much sense for a small company because such an operation would not generate enough cash."
Loge said the company wanted to have enough cash for a four/five year investment programme, as well as to be in a position to acquire a Belgian or foreign competitor.
